hooks.name: Money stays integer cents
hooks.description: When normalize.ts, diff.ts or rules.ts is saved, restate the integer-cents rule for money and ask for a unit test that proves it.

action.prompt: You just saved template/src/normalize.ts, diff.ts or rules.ts. Check the change against the Ghost Watcher money rule: money is an integer number of minor units (`amountMinor`, cents), never a floating-point amount. Parse the whole and fractional digit strings into integers (BigInt is fine) with no Number(...) / 100 and no Math.round(x * 100) / 100 on parsed digits. Store, compare and subtract cents, so a money delta is an exact integer number of cents. Convert cents to a currency string only at the edge (summary sentences, alert emails, the dashboard) with formatMinor. App authors still write dollars in where.* filters and minDelta, and the template converts those targets exactly with compareMinorToMajor or compareToTarget. If this edit touches any money parsing, comparison, delta, filter or formatting code, add or update a Vitest test in template/test/money.test.ts that covers it, including one case that floating point gets wrong (for example $0.10 to $0.30 must give a delta of exactly 20 cents, and $4.35 must parse to 435 cents). Then run `npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit` and fix any failure. If the edit does not touch money, say so in one sentence and stop.
